producer_report.summary: I moved the planning code into run/planning.rs and the pin and reread code into run/pin.rs, with no behavior change. The text was copied by line range, not retyped. The only edits to it are `pub(super)` on four methods that mod.rs still calls (plan_round, stop_planning, pin_repo, reread_after_configuration_change), plus `use super::*;` and a one-line `//!` doc at the top of each new file. mod.rs now declares `mod pin; mod planning;`. No re-exports were needed, because nothing outside run/ named any moved item. The `planning_grant_tests` module moved with `planning_grant`; its tests now run under `run::planning::planning_grant_tests`, names unchanged. CHANGELOG.md has an R3 entry under Unreleased saying there is no behavior change. I ran clippy, the two moved tests and `cargo test -p xtask --test policy`. All passed. I did not run the full `cargo test --locked`.

open_issues: The full `cargo test --locked` was not run by me. It is left to Athena's checks.
learnings: The Planning and Pin rows were methods inside `impl Athena` in run/mod.rs. They moved as `impl Athena` blocks in child modules, and `use super::*;` gives them the parent's imports.
Nothing outside run/ referenced any moved name, and every moved item was private, so mod.rs needs no `pub(crate) use` re-exports.
Bash cannot copy file text, so I split the file with a throwaway Rust program in a temporary directory inside the working directory and deleted it afterwards.
